title: Untrustworthy Website Exposure and Election Beliefs: Selective Exposure and Ideological Asymmetry
screen_reason: Two-wave panel with YouGov Pulse web-tracking of 1,194 US adults around the 2020 election; the paper reports the behavioural share of participants who visited at least one untrustworthy website during the 11-week wave-2 window (39.6%). That is a REACH estimate from behavioural data. The belief associations (17.3%, 4.2%, 12.6%) are effect estimates and are not extractable.

estimates.platform: Web browsing across all websites (YouGov Pulse tracking)
estimates.date: 19 September to 7 December 2020 (wave 2 of web-browsing data)
estimates.measure_type: % of tracked panellists who visited at least one untrustworthy website (domain-level list) during the 11-week wave-2 window
estimates.denominator: 1,194 American adults recruited by YouGov who completed both surveys and had YouGov Pulse web-tracking installed (N = 21M browsing observations)
estimates.definition: Coded 1 if the participant made any recorded page view to a URL within any of 1,796 listed untrustworthy domains between 19 September and 7 December 2020
estimates.misinfo_def: an expanded list of domains from NewsGuard ... classified as 'repeatedly publishing false content' during the 2020 study period
estimates.source_quote: In our data, 39.6% (95% CI [36.8, 42.4]) of our participants were exposed to at least one untrustworthy website in Wave 2.
estimates.page_loc: Section 5 'Untrustworthy Website Exposure and Belief Relationship Estimation Results', p. 9
estimates.ground_truth_detail: A 1,796-domain list built for the 2020 US election context: the Guess, Nyhan & Reifler (2020) list (490 domains from Grinberg et al. 2019 plus 66 from Allcott & Gentzkow 2017) plus 1,240 domains that NewsGuard (an organisation of journalists who rate news sources) classified as 'repeatedly publishing false content' during the study period.
estimates.moderator_quote: Our primary independent variable, binary untrustworthy website exposure, was coded “1” if a participant visited at least one unique domain from this list during the Wave 2 observation period (September 19, 2020, to December 7, 2020), and “0” otherwise. Any recorded page view to a URL within a listed domain constituted a visit.
estimates.notes: Reach over an 11-week window, so the figure is window-dependent; wave 1 (24 Aug-18 Sep 2020) exposure is used as a covariate but its share is never reported. The 39.6% appears to be the unweighted sample share (YouGov survey weights are stated to be applied in the regression analyses, not here). breadth blank because classification is source-level. topic coded politics_elections: the domain list was assembled specifically for the 2020 US election context and the study is an election study, though the listed domains are untrustworthy news domains rather than election-topic-restricted content.

missed_or_uncertain: Not extracted: 19.7% of participants believing Trump was the rightful winner (belief, excluded by protocol); the 17.3% raw and 4.2%/12.6%/-0.2% adjusted associations with belief, and the dosage coefficients (effect estimates, not prevalence); 'exposure dosage' (count of page views to listed domains) is defined but never reported as a mean or a share of browsing, so no intensity/diet-share row is possible. No concentration statistic (top-X% of users accounting for Y% of visits) is reported for this sample - the concentration sentences in the introduction cite other papers and R8 forbids keeping a figure cited from elsewhere.

rob.design: Two-wave YouGov panel (surveys 18 Sep and 7 Dec 2020) of 1,194 US adults with YouGov Pulse web-tracking over two windows (24 Aug-18 Sep; 19 Sep-7 Dec 2020), 21M page-view observations; exposure measured at domain level against a 1,796-domain untrustworthy list (Guess/Grinberg/Allcott + NewsGuard); YouGov survey weights available and applied in the regression models; participants consented and were compensated; IRB approved; data and code on OSF.
rob.item6_quote: To identify participant visits to untrustworthy websites, we followed the procedure used in recent studies (Moore, Dahlke, and Hancock 2023; W. Ahmad et al. 2024) by creating a comprehensive list of 1,796 domains for the 2020 US election context.
rob.item10_quote: In our data, 39.6% (95% CI [36.8, 42.4]) of our participants were exposed to at least one untrustworthy website in Wave 2.
